problem: Our gallery needs a security console: every visitor entering a room is logged generically, but when a curator walks in, the room should additionally record an official inspection under the curator's name and count how many rooms they inspected. Run one tourist and one curator through two rooms and show the difference.

Model hospital ward doors for our ICU and General wards: when a nurse or doctor badges in, print their badge ID; family visitors trigger no ward response at all. Track how many wards each person entered during their shift.

Simulate a cave expedition through three chained chambers (Mouth, Tunnel, Crystal Cavern). Print ENTER as the explorer reaches each chamber and EXIT when they leave it, so the transcript shows departures unwinding in reverse order of arrival.

Roll up budgets across our org chart (HQ containing Engineering with Backend and Frontend, plus Sales): each unit's subtotal is its own budget plus all its sub-units' finalized subtotals, computed bottom-up as the auditor backs out of each unit. Print each unit's subtotal as it completes and the company total.

Guests at our hotel walk past service desks (spa session, room-service dinner, express laundry); each desk adds its price to whichever guest is currently passing by. Print each charge as it happens and what each guest owes at checkout.

In our warehouse simulation, packing stations announce which robot they are serving while robots announce each station they stop at. Count stops per robot and boxes packed per station across a three-station line.

Build a toll plaza collector for gate G-4: cars pay $2.50, trucks pay $2.50 plus 50 cents per ton, motorcycles pay $1.00. Print one payment line per vehicle describing it, and report the revenue collected after the sweep.

Audit a rental shop's media shelf: books are shelved showing title and author, DVDs show title and runtime, and anything unclassified (like an old archive reel) falls through to default handling. Count total items audited and how many needed the default path.

Patrol two factory zones with one monitoring routine that handles both temperature sensors (alert above 75 C) and smoke sensors (alert above 50 ppm). Print every reading as nominal or an alert, and summarize the alert list at the end.

A maintenance crew tours our orchard groves servicing irrigation pumps and sprinklers: one shared routine should log each device kind, how many hours it sat idle, reset its counter, and report the total devices serviced.

Run a moderation sweep over game accounts: member accounts are audited normally, admin accounts get their reputation boosted by 5, and the welcome desk greets every bot passing through no matter what kind of walker it is.

Run feeding rounds at a wildlife park: the info kiosk greets every tour party regardless of who they are, zookeepers feed each animal its species-appropriate meal (meat for lions, seed for parrots, standard feed otherwise), and school groups just watch the animals.

Crawl a small social graph: for each profile list who they timed-follow and what they posted, stamping how long each timed follow has been active during edge traversal itself, and never crawl the same profile twice even though some profiles are reachable by several paths.

Read a chat channel's reactions: show which account reacted to each message via reaction edges, covering moderator pins (only moderators can create them), echoes, and plain reactions from regular users.

Compare a standard courier and an express courier over the same depot chain (HUB, MID, AIR). The express courier overrides depot handling to expedite double the parcels. Print pickup lines for both and their totals.

Health-inspect a restaurant kitchen line (grill, fryer, cold prep): check each station's temperature, flagging anything above 40 C as a violation, and separately log every station visit. Both checks must run at every station.

Enforce clearance levels in our data center: each server room posts the level required, technicians walking the corridor are granted or denied per room, and anyone denied ends their walkthrough immediately without reaching deeper rooms. Report how many rooms each technician reached.

Operate a metro line with two roles: drivers hear station announcements and accumulate track distance as they actually traverse each rail segment, while inspectors only check signage station-by-station and cover no distance.

Simulate a day at the midway: riders too short for the Viper coaster are turned away for the rest of their outing, rides award fun points, and food stalls and gift shops ring up purchases with receipts. Summarize fun points and spending for one tall and one short guest.

Build a dungeon crawler: heroes loot treasure rooms, take damage from traps (collapsing ends the run), retreat from bosses that are too strong, and as they back out each chamber reports its complete subtree gold bottom-up. A rogue subclass sneaks the same dungeon for double loot without fighting.
